action: Credit union members should watch for payment fraud and phishing that uses saved payee details. Credit unions should confirm what Wellington IT holds for them and ask it for access logs.
date_note: Reported Nov 18; the attack ran October 2 to 4, 2026.
exec: A shared IT supplier exposed saved payee records for about 40 Irish credit unions; the supplier's notices say it lacks activity logs to confirm which payees were affected.
plain: A Belfast software supplier used by Irish credit unions was hacked, exposing members' saved payee details such as names and bank account numbers.

key_findings: Wellington IT supplies about 50 credit unions, 43 in Ireland; about 40 affected, at least six have disclosed.
An automated script made five million requests exploiting an authorization flaw with valid credentials, October 2 to 4.
Saved payee records exposed; passwords, PINs and card details reportedly not.
recommendations: Watch for payment fraud and phishing.

summary: About 40 Irish credit unions are affected by a breach at Belfast supplier Wellington IT; BleepingComputer says an automated script exploited an authorization flaw with valid credentials around October 2 to 4. The Register says credit unions report the flaw was closed on October 6. Saved payee records were exposed; passwords and PINs were not. The Irish Times reported it could affect as many as 1.8 million people. Minister Robert Troy called the delay unacceptable.
title: Around 40 Irish credit unions hit by Wellington IT supplier breach

validation.note: Compared BleepingComputer with RTE: about 40 credit unions, breach in October, credit unions told November 17, Troy called delay not acceptable, Wellington IT working with DPC, NCSC and Garda. RTE does not give the request count or dates; other outlets report differing figures (1.4 million vs five million requests, October 2-4 vs October 6), so those are attributed to BleepingComputer only. Follow-up 22 November: The Irish Times (17 November) says more than 40 credit unions (43 in its headline) and up to 1.8 million people potentially affected, its own estimate; it says Wellington IT was contacted and reports no reply. No later statement from Wellington IT found.

review.note: Facts match BleepingComputer, Register, RTE (about 40, Belfast, Oct 2-4, five million requests per BleepingComputer, Oct 6 per Register, Troy); removed occurred_at 08:00Z that no source states

evidence.quote: the potential breach could impact as many as 1.8 million people or over half of the credit union members in Ireland.
